commands.name: manifest
commands.summary: This table as JSON, plus schemaVersion.

commands.name: status
commands.replyShape: {version, sha, engines:{swapd:{enabled,registered}, cliproxy:{enabled,registered,keyPresent}, 9router:{enabled,registered,keyPresent}}, badge, signInRunning, playground, forkTunnel:{enabled, port, state, url?, hostname?}}
commands.summary: App version, which engines are on, engine badge, whether a sign-in is running, the fork server's tunnel (Mac only; state off|invalidPort|blocked|unavailable|starting|up|stopped, url while up — the stable fork_tunnel_hostname on the named tunnel when set, else a quick tunnel).

commands.name: fleets
commands.replyShape: [{key, engineID, provider, capabilities:[String], caveat?, activeNumber?, nextCandidate?, candidateOrder?, nextRecovery?, accounts:[Account], headroom?:{state:abundant|low|critical, window, pct, reason}}]
commands.summary: Every fleet with accounts, usage, active/next, the engine's capabilities and, while priority_mode is on, its headroom verdict (#616: absent = mode off or no usage seen yet; a transient usage gap keeps the last verdict; #743: the interrupt mode says critical where hold says low).

commands.name: plan
commands.summary: The reset battle plan (#7) the planner proposes right now — ignite / switch / hold / reset steps with epoch instants — or null when there is nothing to plan.

commands.name: forecast
commands.replyShape: {forecast: {computedAt, active: <line> | null, accounts: [<line>], allDeadAt, drainOrder: [number], basis} | null} where <line> = {number, email, alias, active, disabled, windows:[{name, pct, ratePctPerHour, resetsAt, hitsAt}]}
commands.summary: Run-rate projection: per account and window the measured pct/hour and the epoch instant it hits 100% (null when the reset lands first or the pace is unknown), the active account's line, and when the fleet's weekly headroom is gone at the active pace with the drain order assumed. Estimates.

commands.name: refresh
commands.summary: Poll every engine now; replies like `fleets`.

commands.name: quit
commands.summary: Quit the menu-bar app gracefully: tunnels, terminals, the engine supervisor and owned sessions are stopped first (#654, the fork's quit-with-window setting).

commands.name: switch
commands.summary: Make account n the active one (proxy: top priority tier).

commands.name: rotate
commands.summary: Switch to the engine's next candidate — what auto-rotation would do now.

commands.name: hold
commands.summary: Take account n out of rotation.

commands.name: unhold
commands.summary: Return account n to rotation.

commands.name: crashes
commands.replyShape: {crashes: [{id, platform, device, at, kind, reason, frames}]}
commands.summary: Crash reports of the phone app (MetricKit, over the mirror) and this Mac app, newest first, without the raw diagnostic.

commands.name: randomize-names
commands.summary: Give every account in the fleet — or only account n, skipping the names the fleet already wears — a fresh name from the current theme's pool (every built-in's when the theme has none).

commands.name: rename
commands.summary: Set (empty string clears) the alias every frontend shows.

commands.name: prefer
commands.summary: Star/unstar an account: the engine lands on starred ones first when it switches (swapd prefer; proxy priority tier). Refused when the engine reports no flag for the account.

commands.name: aws-logins
commands.replyShape: {logins: [{profile, provider?, flow, pid, sessionLabel, state: {phase, url, userCode, message, startedAt} | null}]}
commands.summary: Sessions whose AWS or gcloud sign-in lapsed (the expired-credentials signature in their newest tool results), each with the flow the phone would start and any login in flight; `provider` is "gcloud" for gcloud items and absent for AWS.

commands.name: aws-login
commands.summary: Run the AWS sign-in for a profile and report the URL to open on another device: the relay flow (plain `aws login`, the phone's browser intercepts the localhost callback → `aws-login-callback`), the SSO device-code flow for sso_session profiles, or --remote (`aws login --remote`, code pasted back via `aws-login-code`); --local opens this Mac's browser instead; --status only reports the profile's login and starts nothing. Watch `aws-logins` for the state.

commands.name: aws-login-callback
commands.summary: Relay flow: feed the redirect the phone's browser intercepted (read from stdin) to the waiting login — `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/oauth/callback?code=…` for `aws login`, `http://localhost:8085/?code=…` for `gcloud auth login`; the Mac replays it against the CLI's own listener.

commands.name: aws-login-code
commands.summary: Feed the authorization code read from stdin to the waiting `aws login --remote` for that profile.

commands.name: gcloud-login
commands.summary: Run the gcloud sign-in for an account (`gcloud auth login`, or `auth application-default login` for application-default) and report the URL to open on another device: the relay flow (the phone's browser intercepts the localhost:8085 callback → `aws-login-callback`), or --remote (`--no-launch-browser`, the page ends with a verification code pasted back via `gcloud-login-code`); --local opens this Mac's browser instead; --status only reports the login and starts nothing. Watch `aws-logins` for the state (provider "gcloud").

commands.name: gcloud-login-code
commands.summary: Feed the verification code read from stdin to the waiting `gcloud auth login` for that account.

commands.name: ignite
commands.summary: Start account n's 5h window now with one tiny request (swapd ignite, #7); the active account is untouched. Costs ~1K weekly tokens on n.

commands.name: reorder
commands.summary: Set the rotation order: every account number exactly once, top first.

commands.name: remove
commands.summary: Delete the credential from the engine. Refused without --yes.

commands.name: add
commands.summary: Open the in-app sign-in for this fleet. A human completes it in the Infinitus window; poll with wait-add.

commands.name: wait-add
commands.summary: Block until the running sign-in finishes.

commands.name: signin-begin
commands.summary: Start this fleet's sign-in with no window on the Mac: the reply carries the OAuth URL for the caller to show (the desktop app, #677). Poll signin-status; hand the code back with signin-code.

commands.name: signin-status
commands.summary: Where the sign-in stands; error carries the CLI's own rejection wording.

commands.name: signin-code
commands.summary: Hand the code from the OAuth success page (stdin, never argv) to the waiting sign-in; ok:false carries the CLI's rejection.

commands.name: signin-cancel
commands.summary: Stop the sign-in and close its CLI.

commands.name: windows
commands.replyShape: [{number, title, class, visible, occluded, level, size:[w,h], content}]
commands.summary: Every AppKit window the app owns: title, class, visible, occluded, content view — the e2e/perf probe.

commands.name: events
commands.replyShape: [{id, at, kind, icon, text}] | with --after {after, known, rows:[…]}
commands.summary: The app's event log (switches, deaths, revivals, nudges…), oldest first — what the Activity pane shows. Last 100 kept. --after <event id> returns only the rows past that event; known:false means the id is gone (app relaunched or aged out) and rows is the full tail.

commands.name: stats
commands.replyShape: {period, from, to, total:{humanMessages, phoneMessages, agentMessages, commits, linesAdded, linesRemoved, prsOpened, prsMerged, sessionTally, toolCalls:{name:n}, waitingSeconds, switches, limitStops, usd, …}, previous:{…}, daily:[{key, day}], streak}
commands.summary: Engineering metrics for a period (day|week|month|year, default week): commits, lines, PRs, human/phone/agent messages, sessions, tool calls, waiting time, switches, cost — Stats tab data.

commands.name: utilization
commands.replyShape: {days, bucketSeconds, samples:[{t, email, number, active?, fiveHour?:{pct, resetsAt}, sevenDay?:{pct, resetsAt}, scoped?:{name:{pct, resetsAt}}}], generations:[{email, window, resetAt, finalPct, observationGap}], fiveHourWindows:[{email, number?, start, resetsAt, peakPct, samples, closed}], replay:{from, to, switches, coldSwitches, stalledSeconds, sawActiveFlag}, dryRunPlan?, windows:[name], emails:[email], rates?:{computedAt, lastHour:{input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, usd, messages}, lastDay, lastWeek, files, unpricedModels}, liveRate?:{perMinute, peakPerMinute}}
commands.summary: The Utilization pane's data over the last N days (default 7): the recorded usage samples downsampled to the pane's bucket, weekly-window waste generations, five-hour windows, the replay report, the dry-run plan, and the transcript token run rate.

commands.name: perf
commands.replyShape: {cpuSeconds, rssBytes, heapBytes, threads, uptimeSeconds, leases, leaseScopes: {clientId: [scope]}}
commands.summary: Process cost: CPU seconds so far, RSS + live heap bytes, thread count — sample twice for an idle % and a heap growth rate (perf gate).

commands.name: lock-status
commands.replyShape: {enabled, locked, relock: immediately|5 min|1 h|on sleep}
commands.summary: Biometric lock (Settings › Lock): whether the setting is on, whether the pop-out and Settings are locked right now, and the re-lock choice. Off by default.

commands.name: lock
commands.summary: Biometric lock: `on` runs the unlock prompt on the Mac once and turns the setting on; `off` turns it off (--yes while in a team); `now` locks the pop-out and Settings; `relock <choice>` sets the re-lock delay.

commands.name: unlock
commands.summary: Run the unlock prompt on the Mac (Touch ID or password) and unlock the pop-out and Settings; refused with the reason when it fails or is cancelled.

commands.name: team-status
commands.replyShape: {id, name, remote (masked), kid, role: leader|member|pending, rev, members: [{kid, name, role, isMe, founder, lastPublished, kinds, sessionsNow, blockers, crashes, todayUSD, todayMessages, todayCommits, fleet, controls}], requests: [{kid, name, platform, devices, at}], lastFetch, lastPublish, lastError} | null
commands.summary: Settings › Team: the team this Mac is in — members with what they last published, today's effort and blockers, pending requests, the loop's last fetch/publish — or null when there is none.

commands.name: team-create
commands.summary: Create a team on an empty git remote; the remote's write token, if it needs one, comes on stdin (empty stdin: none).

commands.name: team-join
commands.summary: Request to join a team: the team code or invite link on stdin, this Mac's name in the roster as the argument.

commands.name: team-hostname
commands.summary: Settings › Team › Hostnames: keep the Cloudflare zone and label member hostnames are minted under, with the API token on stdin (checked against the zone before it is kept); --clear forgets the token.

commands.name: team-code
commands.summary: Mint a team code (leaders): `infinitus://join/…`, valid --days (default 7); --invite adds a one-time nonce the app auto-approves when Settings › Team's switch is on (off by default). Carries the store credential when one is set.

commands.name: team-fetch
commands.summary: Pull the store now (roster, members' files, requests) and rebuild the snapshot.

commands.name: team-publish
commands.summary: Publish this Mac's data now (what the 5-minute loop does), then rebuild the snapshot.

commands.name: team-compact
commands.summary: Rewrite your own member branch to a single commit without the pre-split transcript history — the one force-push the spec allows, explicit and once; teammates' mirrors follow on their next fetch.

commands.name: team-approve
commands.summary: Approve a join request (leaders).

commands.name: team-decline
commands.summary: Decline a join request (leaders).

commands.name: show
commands.summary: Open a window: the pinned pop-out or Settings. The wall, workspace and session windows are retired — the Infinitus desktop app is the client.

commands.name: prefs
commands.summary: The preference catalog with current values: key, type, default, section (slug + name), live/restart effect, choices; `get` narrows it to the named keys.

commands.name: activities-token
commands.summary: Register a phone's push token — the body `POST /activities/token` takes: {kind, token, deviceId, deviceName, environment, themeID?, macId?}. Without --body the CLI reads the JSON from stdin. `--forget <deviceId>/<kind>` withdraws that one registration instead (the phone's alerts switched off); forgotten is false when none was held.

commands.name: client-activity
commands.summary: A client's visibility report — the body `POST /client-activity` takes: {clientId, visible, focused, recentlyInteracted, scopes:[{type:sessions|session|fleets|stats, pid?}], ttlMs}. Leases the scopes it watches.

commands.name: crash-report
commands.summary: File a client's crash or hang — the body `POST /crashes` takes: {id, platform, device, appVersion, osVersion, at (ISO-8601), kind, reason, frames, raw?}; `crashes` lists it.

commands.name: prefs-set
commands.summary: Set one preference (`prefs set <key> <value>` is the same): the value is JSON, or a bare word for a string; refused when it is the wrong type or off the pref's choices. A `restart` pref relaunches the app after the reply, as `engine` does.

commands.name: hide
commands.summary: Close the pinned pop-out (the e2e no-lease window) or Settings.

commands.name: engine
commands.summary: Turn an engine on or off. The app relaunches.

commands.name: proxy
commands.summary: CLIProxyAPI settings: base URL, whether a key is stored, routing strategy.

commands.name: proxy-key
commands.summary: Store the management key read from stdin in the keychain. Empty stdin clears it. The app relaunches.

commands.name: 9router-password
commands.summary: Store the 9Router dashboard password read from stdin in the keychain. Empty stdin clears it. The app relaunches.

commands.name: proxy-routing
commands.summary: PUT the proxy's routing strategy.

commands.name: team-grants
commands.replyShape: {schema, grants: [{id, audience, sessions, capabilities, preauthorized?, since, expires?}]}
commands.summary: This Mac's session-control grants (#220): who may do what to which sessions.

commands.name: team-grant
commands.replyShape: {id, audience, sessions, capabilities, preauthorized?, since, expires?}
commands.summary: Add a grant: the capabilities in --cap for the people named on the sessions named (all when --sessions is absent); --pre names the ones that run without asking (delete never does); --expires counts from now.

commands.name: team-revoke
commands.summary: Remove one grant; the next command under it is refused noGrant.

commands.name: team-discoverable
commands.summary: Advertise this Mac to teams on the LAN (TXT d=1, /team/key and /team/request), or hide it.

commands.name: event
commands.summary: A Claude Code hook payload on stdin (the plugin's Notification/Stop hooks): a prompt is pushed the moment it appears, then the fleet refreshes.

commands.name: approve
commands.summary: A PreToolUse hook payload on stdin: {decision: allow} when the phone allowed that tool for this session, else {decision: ask}.

commands.name: sessions
commands.replyShape: [{pid, name?, cwd, status?, kind, profile?, permissionMode?, sessionId, account?, startedAt?, needs}]
commands.summary: The live Claude Code sessions: pid, name, folder, status, session id, the account alias they run on, start time (ISO 8601) and pending sign-in needs (`aws-login:<profile>`, `gcloud-login:<account>`).

commands.name: nudge
commands.summary: Sends one session the resume nudge by hand (peer socket first, then its terminal); {nudged: false, reason} when its transcript does not end in a limit stop or it cannot be reached.

commands.name: profiles
commands.replyShape: {profiles: [{name, cwd?, engine?, permissionMode?, model?, systemPrompt?, prompt?, allowTools?}]}
commands.summary: The saved session profiles (Settings › Profiles): name, folder, engine, permission mode, model, system prompt, first prompt.

commands.name: profile-set
commands.summary: Creates or replaces a session profile with exactly the fields given (an omitted field is cleared). --allow lists tools a session born from it runs without asking (the plugin's PreToolUse hook).

commands.name: profile-remove
commands.summary: Deletes a session profile.

commands.name: checkpoints
commands.summary: The session's per-prompt workspace checkpoints (hidden git refs), oldest first.

commands.name: checkpoint-diff
commands.summary: Checkpoint n against checkpoint m, or against the working tree now (untracked files included): a --stat and the patch (capped at 200 KB).

commands.name: checkpoint-restore
commands.replyShape: {restored: {n, sha, at, subject}, backup?: {n, sha, at, subject}}
commands.summary: Puts the repository's files back to checkpoint n (the current state is checkpointed first, so it is undoable). Needs --yes.

commands.name: past-sessions
commands.replyShape: {sessions: [{sessionId, cwd, repo, firstMessage, lastActivityAt, bytes, live}]}
commands.summary: Every Claude Code session this Mac has run, newest first (default 50): id, folder, opening prompt, last activity, whether it is live. --search filters that newest set by repo, folder or prompt.

commands.name: resume-session
commands.summary: Opens a new terminal in the folder that past session ran in and resumes it there (claude --resume), like the phone's Start session. --fork continues from the transcript under a new session id (claude --fork-session), leaving the original alone — allowed on a live session.

commands.name: session-mode
commands.summary: Moves a running session's permission mode for the plugin's PreToolUse hook: Auto-accept edits allows the editing tools, Full access every tool, supervised clears it. A mode set at start is a floor — it cannot be narrowed from here.

commands.name: send
commands.summary: Text on stdin goes to that session as if typed into its prompt (peer socket first, then its terminal).
